why: Sentence verified verbatim (user-input.md line 15), but the WHOLE line reverses the finding: 'The callback can stay pending indefinitely. Execution remains paused until your callback returns, and the SDK only cancels the wait when the query itself is cancelled. If a user might take longer to respond than your process can reasonably stay running, return the defer hook decision...'. Pending-forever is the documented NORM; defer is the conditional alternative for a process that cannot stay running. The identifier half of the claim is true (ClaudePreToolUseHookPipelineResult.hookDecision at claude-agent.ts:145 is typed 'allow' | 'ask' only, runClaudePreToolUseHookPipeline at :177 drops any other decision, the checkResult switch at :1450-1571 emits only allow/modify/block/ask/prompt, and grep -a finds no tool_deferred or deferred_tool_use anywhere under packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/). The CONSEQUENCE is false on two independent grounds. (1) One layer up, R7 Task 4 already provides exactly the capability defer exists to provide, and it is backend-agnostic: SessionManager.ts:12694 assigns managed.agent.onPermissionRequest = request => this.handleAgentPermissionRequest(managed, request) on the generic agent, and ClaudeAgent's case 'prompt' (claude-agent.ts:1518-1571) publishes through it; that handler persists PiPendingApprovalV1 into managed.pendingApproval (SessionManager.ts:6410-6430; 'pendingApproval' is in SESSION_PERSISTENT_FIELDS, sessions/types.ts:48), reprojectPendingApproval (:6622) re-fires the prompt through the production PermissionRequest band on open after restart, and settleDurableApproval (:6674) settles it with no live agent, an ALLOW re-driving the interrupted turn. The parity audit R7 row records this live-proven under CDP pass 11: a pending consent survives a SIGKILL, re-fires on open, and completes. So a Claude-backend approval that outlives the host process does have an exit, and it does not require cancelling the query. (2) The mechanism itself is scoped away from this surface by Claude's own contract: hooks.md:1587 states defer 'is for integrations that run claude -p as a subprocess and read its JSON output... Claude Code honors this value only in non-interactive mode with the -p flag. In interactive sessions it logs a warning and ignores the hook result.' Nessy's Pi implementation mirrors that gate exactly (pi-agent.ts:3872-3878, gated on this.config.isHeadless and on a single-tool-call turn), so 'the defer round trip exists on the Pi backend only' actually means 'on the headless surface only' — Pi does not defer in the desktop app either. On the interactive Claude surface the documented behavior IS to ignore a defer, which is what the pipeline does (a defer decision is neither block nor allow/ask at :167/:177, so the call falls through the normal permission flow). The claimed evidence line range is also off: claude-agent.ts:1428-1434 is the steer-message/continueWith block, not the decision translation. The only genuine residue is cosmetic/edge — no warning is logged when an ignored defer arrives, and a headless run on the Claude backend would not produce tool_deferred termination — neither of which is the claimed consequence.
correctedState: Nessy's Claude backend implements the documented default: the PreToolUse callback stays pending indefinitely while the approval is surfaced to the user (claude-agent.ts:1518-1571). It never emits permissionDecision:'defer' and never consumes deferred_tool_use — which matches Claude's own rule that defer is honored only in non-interactive `claude -p` runs and is warned-and-ignored in interactive sessions (hooks.md:1587); Nessy's Pi defer is gated on isHeadless for the same reason, so the mechanism is headless-only on both backends, not Pi-only. An approval that outlives the host process is handled one layer up and backend-agnostically by R7 durable approvals: the prompt is persisted as pendingApproval, the process may exit, and on restart + session open reprojectPendingApproval re-fires it through the production PermissionRequest band with settleDurableApproval re-driving the interrupted turn on ALLOW (live-proven against SIGKILL, CDP pass 11). Residual, both minor and outside the claim: an ignored defer from a trusted PreToolUse hook is dropped silently instead of logging a warning, and a headless Claude-backend run would not terminate with tool_deferred.
